name: Garden of Eden
hook: Four rivers, one forbidden fruit and a couple expelled: Eden's clues stay in Genesis.

facts.label: Genesis
facts.statement: In Genesis, God plants Eden and puts Adam there "to dress it and keep it"; the name is Hebrew for "pleasure" or "delight."

facts.label: its four rivers
facts.statement: Four rivers flow out of Eden: the Pison, Gihon, Hiddekel (Tigris) and Euphrates; Babylon later rose on the Euphrates.

facts.label: Adam and Eve
facts.statement: Adam and Eve are the first couple; after eating the forbidden fruit they are expelled, and an archangel with a sword guards the way back.

facts.label: Cain and Seth
facts.statement: Cain kills his brother Abel and is exiled to the land of Nod, east of Eden; Seth is the third son born to Adam and Eve.

facts.label: Paradise Lost
facts.statement: Milton's 1667 epic Paradise Lost retells the Fall, with the angel Michael leading Adam and Eve out of Eden.

facts.label: paradise
facts.statement: Eden became a synonym for any ideal place; "paradise" comes from an ancient Persian word for an enclosed park.

facts.label: Ask and Embla
facts.statement: In Scandinavian mythology, Ask and Embla are the first man and woman, the Norse counterparts of Adam and Eve.
